articleTitle: Human factors and the computer-integrated manufacturing enterprise
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The management of manufacturing increasingly makes use of information technology, and concomitantly the role of human factors has grown. From the perspective of managing engineering technology, the author identifies four of the trends currently being introduced into British Industry: total quality, the distributed enterprise, communications and the software engineered manufacturing organisation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flexible work practices for flexible manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The author looks at the organisational changes and the change of attitude on the shop floor required for the introduction of FMS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sample application of the human-centered design philosophy in a CIM system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The paper summarizes the main principles of the philosophy of human-centred design of man-machine and manufacturing systems, and illustrates the realization of this concept by describing its application in a particular case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Human factors in CIM: a European perspective
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The paper enumerates some of the business and competitive pressures that are at work in manufacturing, which are slowly bringing about an increased awareness that the success of CIM lies not in removing or incapacitating shopfloor employees, but in handing over to them significant amounts of decision making authority and control. It describes the concept of human-centered CIM and the research and development work that has been undertaken in this area is mentioned, including projects funded by the Commission of the European Communities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aspects of an experimental industrial application of a human-centered CIM system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The paper, by reference to an experimental industrial application of human-centered computer integrated manufacturing (HC-CIM) systems attempts to outline a new, more balanced approach, a balance between technology, organisation and the greatest asset any company possesses, its people. It is an approach in which technology is shaped around people and not where people are fitted around the technology viz. the human-centered approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Human considerations of AGV utilisation in multi-product batch manufacture
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The use of AGV's in batch manufacturing requires extensive changes to the job design of employees, to individual areas of responsibility and to the organisational structure. Due to the importance of the man/machine interfaces, co-operation of employees is essential, and any erroneous attitude by senior management, who might aim at investment justification by labour replacement will cause industrial relations problems. Without co-operation, AGV investment will not attain the desired benefits and may become a bad investment. In addition, senior management need to realise the extent of changes required in the factory and other departments in the company.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Problems of designing task-based user interfaces for large-scale CIM systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Human Factor in CIM
abstract: The paper describes the methodology adopted within a major Alvey project, 'design to product' (DtoP), to design a series of user interfaces for a range of AI-based tools and their accompanying utilities. It moves on to discuss some of the major issues and problems that arose during the development of these interfaces and some of the conclusions reached by the HUSAT team during the project.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
